chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah al-Himyari narrated to me from his father, from Harun ibn Muslim, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Ash'ath, from 'Abdillah ibn Hammad al-Ansari, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him say: The grave of al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him) is twenty cubits by twenty cubits, divided; it is a garden from the gardens of Paradise. And in it [and from it] is the ascension of the angels to the heaven. And there is no angel brought near nor a messenger prophet except that he asks Allah to visit him. So a group descends and a group ascends.
ai.seo_question: What are the dimensions and spiritual significance of Imam Husayn's grave according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* establishes the physical dimensions of Imam al-Husayn’s (a.s.) grave as twenty by twenty cubits, characterizing it as a 'garden of Paradise' and a spiritual axis (*mi'raj*) for angels. It underscores the unique status of the Imam in Shia theology, where even appointed prophets and close angels actively seek divine permission to visit, illustrating the continuous flow of spiritual connection between the celestial and terrestrial realms.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 3. Muḥammad ibn ‘Abdillāh Al-Ḥimyari narrated to me from his father, from Hārūn ibn Muslim, from (‘Abdillāh ibn ‘Amr) ibn Ash’ath, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Ḥammād Al-Ansāri, from Ibn Sinān, who said:

I heard Abā ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) say: The boundaries of the grave (Ḥaram) of Ḥusain ibn ‘Ali (a.s.) are twenty ells by twenty ells, and this location is a garden from the gardens of Paradise. The ascent of the angels toward the heavens begins from here. Every high-ranked angel and every prophet, who was chosen as a messenger, asks Allāh (at all times) for permission to go to the Ziyārah of Ḥusain (a.s.). (There is always) a crowd descending (from the heavens to go to the Ziyārah of Ḥusain (a.s.)) and a crowd ascending (back).
